note: The registry of every placeholder of the kit. A placeholder is a name in capitals in square brackets, for example [YOUR_NAME]. `npm run setup` asks for each one in this order and fills it in. VARIABLES.md is made from this file: run `npm run setup -- --docs` after a change.

variables.name: YOUR_NAME
variables.meaning: Your full name, as the agents should write it.

variables.name: YOUR_FIRST_NAME
variables.meaning: The name the agents call you in charters, playbooks and skills.

variables.name: MEMO_OWNER
variables.meaning: Your short name in Memo commands: `memo send --to sam`. Small letters, digits and hyphens only; it must start with a letter.

variables.name: YOUR_ORG
variables.meaning: The organisation or business your work is for. For personal use only, write: my own projects.

variables.name: YOUR_ROLE
variables.meaning: Your role there, in a few words.

variables.name: YOUR_EMAIL
variables.meaning: Your work email address: the mailbox the agents read and draft in.

variables.name: YOUR_WORK_DOMAIN
variables.meaning: The part of your work email after the @. Only a calendar on this domain gives meeting follow-ups, so a personal calendar gives none.

variables.name: YOUR_TIMEZONE
variables.meaning: Your time zone, as an IANA name.
variables.default: the time zone of this computer

variables.name: YOUR_CITY
variables.meaning: The place whose sunrise and sunset turn the pages light and dark. A city name, for the tooltip of the Theme button. Skip it and the pages follow Greenwich; the Theme button still holds light or dark.

variables.name: YOUR_LATITUDE
variables.meaning: The latitude of that place, in degrees, north positive. Search the web for: latitude longitude <your city>.

variables.name: YOUR_LONGITUDE
variables.meaning: The longitude of that place, in degrees, east positive (so the Americas are negative).

variables.name: WRITING_STYLE_NOTES
variables.meaning: How you want text written for you to read, in one line. The agents follow it in every memo.
variables.example: Short sentences. The point first. No jargon.
variables.defaultValue: Short sentences. The point first, then the reason. Plain words.

variables.name: MAC_USERNAME
variables.meaning: The account name of your user on the Mac that runs Memo (the name of your home folder). In Terminal on that Mac, the command whoami prints it.

variables.name: MEMO_APP_PATH
variables.meaning: The full path of the app folder of this kit on that Mac. Setup finds it; change it only if you will move the kit.
variables.default: the app folder of this kit

variables.name: VAULT_PATH
variables.meaning: The folder of your vault: the notes that the agents keep about your meetings, mail, people and projects. Setup creates it from vault-template/.

variables.name: AGENT_WORK_DIR
variables.meaning: The folder the agents start in, for their scratch files. Setup creates it.

variables.name: OUTBOX_PATH
variables.meaning: The folder where an agent puts a file that you must open yourself (a PDF, a spreadsheet, a page). Setup creates it.

variables.name: TAILSCALE_HOST
variables.meaning: The full Tailscale name of the Mac that runs Memo. In the Tailscale admin console, on the Machines page, click the Mac: the name ends in .ts.net. Skip it until Tailscale is installed (README step 8), then run setup again.

variables.name: TAILSCALE_LOGIN
variables.meaning: The login name of your Tailscale account: the email address or name at the top right of the Tailscale admin console. Only this login opens Memo with no token.

variables.name: NTFY_TOPIC
variables.meaning: A long random name for phone alerts through the ntfy app, when an agent is blocked. Anyone who knows the name can read the alerts, so make it hard to guess. Skip it for no alerts.

variables.name: MAIN_AGENT_MODEL
variables.meaning: The model of the agent main: a Claude Code model alias (opus, sonnet) or a full model id.

variables.name: SECOND_AGENT_MODEL
variables.meaning: The model of the agent second.

variables.name: HELPER_MODEL
variables.meaning: The default model alias for the helpers (subagents) that read sources and write summaries. A cheaper tier keeps your usage limits for the hard work.

variables.name: FIRST_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL
variables.meaning: The email address of your first Claude account, which runs the agent main.

variables.name: SECOND_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL
variables.meaning: The email address of your second Claude account, which runs the agent second. Skip it if you have one account: both agents then share it and its limits.

variables.name: SECOND_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
variables.meaning: The folder where Claude Code keeps the sign-in of the second account. With one account only, answer ~/.claude.

variables.name: GITHUB_USERNAME
variables.meaning: Your GitHub user name, for the private backup of the vault. Skip it for no backup; the nightly sync then commits on the Mac only.

variables.name: VAULT_GITHUB_REPO
variables.meaning: The private GitHub repository that backs up the vault, as user/name.

variables.name: TASK_MANAGER
variables.meaning: The tool that holds your tasks and is the source of truth for them. It needs a connector on your Claude account.

variables.name: MEETING_NOTES_TOOL
variables.meaning: The tool that records your meetings and gives notes and transcripts. It needs a connector on your Claude account.

variables.name: CHAT_TOOL
variables.meaning: The chat tool of your team.

variables.name: SLACK_CHANNELS_TO_SYNC
variables.meaning: The team channels whose every message the nightly sync saves, with commas between them. Your direct messages and your own threads are saved anyway.

variables.name: SYNC_START_DATE
variables.meaning: How far back the first nightly sync reads your meetings, mail, chat and documents, as YYYY-MM-DD. Later runs go further back when they have room.

variables.name: WHERE_TO_SEND_DRAFTS
variables.meaning: Where an agent leaves a draft for you to review and send. The safe default: a draft inside the tool itself, plus a memo with the full text.
variables.example: a draft in the tool it will be sent from (a Gmail draft, a Slack draft), plus a memo with the full text and the link
variables.defaultValue: a draft in the tool it will be sent from (a Gmail draft, a Slack draft), plus a memo with the full text and the link

variables.name: WHERE_TO_SEND_FOLLOWUPS
variables.meaning: Where meeting follow-ups go by default, when the routing list of the playbook has no row for the meeting.
variables.example: a Slack direct message to the person for a teammate, an email for anyone outside the team
variables.defaultValue: a Slack direct message to the person for a teammate, an email for anyone outside the team

variables.name: SLACK_CHANNEL_FOR_ANNOUNCEMENTS
variables.meaning: The channel for announcements to your whole community or company (the example skill slack-announcement uses it). Skip it if you post none.

variables.name: SLACK_CHANNEL_FOR_TEAM_UPDATES
variables.meaning: The internal channel of your team, for updates and for the follow-up of a team meeting.

variables.name: SIGNED_DOCS_FOLDER
variables.meaning: The Google Drive folder where documents to sign, and their signed copies, live.

variables.name: BOOKING_LINK
variables.meaning: Your scheduling link, which agents put in a reply that proposes a call.

variables.name: NIGHTLY_SYNC_HOUR
variables.meaning: The hour (0 to 23, by the clock of the Mac that runs Memo) at which the agents restart; the nightly sync starts 30 minutes later. Pick an hour when you sleep.

variables.name: DAILY_REVIEW_HOUR
variables.meaning: The hour (0 to 23, by the clock of the Mac that runs Memo) at which the daily review memo arrives, Monday to Friday.

variables.name: MEMO_TOKEN
variables.meaning: The secret token of Memo. Setup makes a random one, writes it only into app/.env, and never shows it. You are not asked for it.
